name: Saudi GID

summary.text: The General Intelligence Presidency (also referred to as the General Intelligence Directorate, GID, or Saudi General Intelligence) is Saudi Arabia's principal foreign intelligence agency. Saudipedia, a Saudi reference site, states it was established in 1956 under King Saud bin Abdulaziz, that its basic law was issued by Royal Decree M-5 in December 1982, and that in 2018 a ministerial committee chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman was formed to restructure it. On this site it appears through Kamal Adham, its former head and a BCCI investor; Prince Bandar bin Sultan, its head from July 2012 to April 2014; and a 2017 FBI memo describing Omar al-Bayoumi as a paid cooptee of the agency.

sources.title: Saudi Crown Prince presides over committee to restructure intelligence agency

facts.claim: Kamal Adham, described by the Washington Post as a former head of Saudi intelligence, pleaded guilty in 1992 in the BCCI case and was a key figure in the 1982 takeover of First American Bankshares.
facts.quote: Adham, former head of Saudi intelligence and a key figure in the 1982 takeover of First American Bankshares Inc.

sources.title: Key BCCI Investor Enters Guilty Plea

facts.claim: Prince Bandar bin Sultan, formerly Saudi ambassador to Washington, was appointed head of Saudi General Intelligence in July 2012. On April 15, 2014 a royal decree published by the Saudi Press Agency relieved him of the post 'at his own request' and asked his deputy, General Youssef al-Idrissi, to carry out the duties of head of general intelligence.
facts.quote: was relieved of his post at his own request and General Youssef Al Idrissi was asked to carry out the duties of the head of general intelligence

sources.title: Saudi intelligence chief Prince Bandar relieved of post
Saudi Arabia: Prince Bandar relieved of intelligence post
Saudi intelligence chief replaced by his deputy

facts.claim: A June 2017 FBI communication, declassified in 2022, states that Omar al-Bayoumi was paid a monthly stipend from the late 1990s until September 2001 as a cooptee of the Saudi General Intelligence Presidency, and that the FBI had confirmed this involvement, which was not established at the time of the 9/11 Commission report. ProPublica reported that FBI documents say he reported to Prince Bandar. Saudi Arabia denies that al-Bayoumi was its asset.
facts.quote: was paid a monthly stipend as a cooptee of the Saudi General Intelligence Presidency (GIP)

facts.claim: In October 2018 Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman chaired the first meeting of a ministerial committee formed to restructure the General Intelligence Presidency; reported measures included new departments for strategy and development, legal affairs and performance appraisal.

openQuestions: The agency's official website (gip.gov.sa) was not reachable; the founding and legal-basis details rest on Saudipedia and should be checked against an official page.
Adham's exact tenure (commonly given as 1965-1979) and Turki al-Faisal's 1979-2001 tenure were found only on Wikipedia and are not recorded here.
The quoted 'cooptee' passage comes from press summaries of the 2017 FBI communication; the FBI Vault release should be checked for the document itself.
